name: purple worm

special_abilities.name: tunneler
special_abilities.desc: The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: The worm makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its stinger.

actions.name: bite
actions.desc:
Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the worm. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the worm, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the worm's turns.
If the worm takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the worm must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the worm. If the worm dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting prone.

actions.name: tail stinger
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 19 (3d6 + 9) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

lore:
Behold the *Vermis Purpureus*, the undisputed titan of the lightless deep. These behemoths carve impossible labyrinths through the crushing weight of the Underdark, devouring solid granite as easily as a common earthworm moves through garden soil. 

Driven by an insatiable, mindless hunger, the worm senses the rhythmic thrum of life through miles of stone. It does not merely hunt; it consumes. Its maw is a grinding abyss of serrated plates, capable of swallowing a pack horse whole, while its tail bears a wicked, vitriol-dripping stinger to dispatch any foe too large for its gullet.

To the mountain-folk, the worm is known as "The World-Eater." In dwarven folklore, its passage is heralded by the "Deep Shiver"—tremors that topple citadels and signal the mountain’s displeasure. They are viewed less as mere beasts and more as a localized apocalypse; to hear the distant, rhythmic grinding of rock is to hear the approach of inevitable doom. For where the Purple Worm travels, the earth itself rises to reclaim what was stolen from the dark.
